terra.problem: The passage does not say the people were proud of being Abraham's descendants.
Papa says he has a history with bills, adding an unsupported detail to his own life. Bills should come up as something people deal with.
The passage does not say what importance this crowd placed on the Law.
The reference to Jesus eating with tax collectors elsewhere needs a Scripture reference.
They do not move from naming Abraham to naming God in one breath. Jesus speaks between their two claims.
The fact about Moses leading Israel out of Egypt needs a Scripture reference.
The fact that David was Israel's king needs a Scripture reference.
The claim about Herod's reputation needs a Scripture reference, and it does not identify which Herod is meant.
The identification of Pharaoh as the king of Egypt who held Israel needs a Scripture reference.
The final sentence changes Jesus's reason from their not believing Him because He speaks the truth to their not believing Him even though He speaks the truth.
The passage does not say the crowd knew the Law well enough to argue about Abraham.
The background claim about Jews looking down on Samaritans needs a Scripture reference.
The claim that Jesus was from Galilee needs a Scripture reference.
The two questions are related, but asking whether Jesus is greater than Abraham is not the same question as asking who He claims to be.
“Ha, I wish” has no clear meaning in response to whether Jesus was richer than Abraham.
“He won't say anything else about the Father” is an unsupported absolute; Jesus says other things about the Father in the passage.
The passage does not establish that the people who pick up stones are the same believers addressed at the beginning.
The passage does not say it is daytime.
The text says Jesus went out, not that He walked out. The explanation adds a detail immediately after saying it will not guess.
This is the last passage in the story group, so the explanation should not say the story isn't over or promise more teaching ahead.
